sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

The present appeal is filed by the appellant - Insurance Company under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 12.4.2024 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, (Main), Bhavnagar in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.131 of 2023, by which, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding Rs.47,43,000/- with 9% p.a. interest to be paid to claimant/s, by holding opponents liable, jointly and severally.

entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
2. The facts of the present appeal are as under :

sentences.text: NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2367/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined

2.1 The claimants filed the claim petition before the learned Tribunal stating that the deceased was driving his Hero Honda Motorcycle bearing registration no.GJ-17L-2741 in a moderate speed and on his correct side and going to Mahindra show room, however, when he reached the spot of occurrence of the accident in question, the opponent no.1 drove the dumper truck bearing registration no.GJ-13W-0712 in a rash and negligent manner endangering human life and dashed with the motorcycle driven by the deceased from behind due to which the deceased fell down and got crushed under the dumper truck and succumbed to the injuries sustained by him in the said vehicular accident.
2.2 The notices were served to the opponents.
The opponents filed the written statement before the learned Tribunal.
The issues were framed by the Tribunal.
Oral as well as documentary evidence were led before the Tribunal.

After hearing the submissions made by the rival parties, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition(s) and awarded compensation as noted above.
2.3
Hence, the insurance company of the dumper involved in the accident has filed the present appeal before this Court.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2367/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined 3.

Learned advocate for the appellant - Insurance Company has submitted that the deceased was not wearing helmet as mandated in the MV Act; that the deceased was riding his motorcycle in zigzag manner and had contributed to the accident and therefore, the learned Tribunal has erred in holding the driver of the dumper negligent to the extent of 100%.
He also submitted that the learned Tribunal has erred in awarding the compensation and the learned Tribunal ought to have considered the multiplier of five only.

He also submitted that the rate of interest awarded at the 9%
is also on the higher side and the learned Tribunal ought to have awarded 7.5%.
He submitted that on all these counts, this appeal is required to be allowed and the impugned judgment and award is required to be modified.
4. I have considered the submissions made by the the learned advocate for the appellant.
I have perused the record and proceedings.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
I have also considered the pleadings of the parties before the Tribunal.

Considering the FIR, panchanama of scene of offence, PM report, inquest panchanama, wherein it is clear that the motorcycle driven by the deceased was lying on the place of accident in damaged condition and also that the driver of the said dumper truck dashed with the motorcycle from behind and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2367/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined that there is no evidence in rebuttal on behalf of the opponents to show that there was also negligence on the part of the deceased and as the tractor was a heavy vehicle, it was the duty of the driver of the said dumper truck to ply his vehicle with utmost care and keeping safe distance from other vehicles, therefore,
the learned Tribunal discussed every point in detail and held the dumper negligent to the extent of 100%.

sentences.text: It is now well settled that multiplier is to be based on age of the deceased in view of the judgment in the case of Joginder Singh V/s ICICI Lombard reported in 2020(18)SCC 808, Rakesh Arora V/s Bharti Axa General Ins.co.Ltd. Reported in 2023 ACJ 337 and Bheemasen Since Deceased Through His Lrs. V/s Aravind Bangar reported in 2024 ACJ 221

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: and therefore, the multiplier of 16 years awarded for age of 30 years of deceased is just and proper.

Further, considering the proof of income of the deceased produced on the record, his age, number of dependents, future prospects, law laid down with regard to the multiplier and conventional heads, the learned Tribunal has awarded the amount of compensation.

6. As regards the ground of rate of interest on the awarded amount, there are several instances where the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2367/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined learned Tribunal has awarded 9% interest and that there is no hard and fast rule to award the rate of interest.

Considering the year of accident and considering the nature of the work done by the deceased and his dependents and also considering the other surrounding circumstances, the Court may exercise discretion without assigning any further reasons.
Normally, the interest rate which is awarded by the Courts in the motor accident claim petitions in the last few years is between 6% to 9% p.a.
Therefore, it cannot be said that where the interest is already awarded at 9% should now be reduced in this appeal.
7. In view of above discussion and as the insurance company has failed to prove its case by leading cogent and convincing reasons, this appeal therefore deserves to be dismissed at admission stage.
8. In view of above, the following order is passed.
8.1 The present appeal and civil application are dismissed with no order as to costs.
8.2 The appellant is directed to deposit the entire awarded amount with costs and interest before the concerned Tribunal within four weeks from today.

After the amount is deposited, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2367/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined the learned Tribunal shall pass the order of disbursement as per the operative portion of the impugned judgment and award within a period of six weeks thereafter.
8.3 Record and proceedings, if any, be sent back to the concerned Tribunal, forthwith.
